sourceKind: public CA incident report filed by the affected operator

evidence.fact: When N domain names required CAA rechecking, Boulder selected one domain and checked it N times instead of checking every domain identity.
CAA had to be checked within eight hours before issuance when a cached domain validation was older than eight hours.
The operator identified 3,048,289 affected currently valid certificates out of approximately 116 million active certificates.
A Go loop-iterator reference error caused the identity collapse; the unit test checked only authorization count, and the integration test used one FQDN, so both missed value-to-domain binding.
Remediation added content checks, a lower-level conversion test, multi-domain integration coverage, log verification, and stronger static analysis.

observedFailure: A multi-identity authorization path preserved cardinality but rebound every check to one identity, while tests asserted count and a one-identity example rather than identity-to-result correspondence.
